//Serilog: EF Core logs every SQL statement under Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Database.Command
at Information, and the Console sink in Program.cs is synchronous - so every
statement the application runs serialises through one lock on the request path.
Measured 2026-09-29 with deploy/load.cs. Without the override below, a host
taking 200 req/s wrote 244,843 log lines in under two minutes and failed 91.5%
of requests (5,493 of 6,000), all at connection establishment - the server
logged nothing, because the requests never reached application code. The
identical run with the override sustained 199.8 req/s with zero errors and
8,010 lines, which is request logging doing its job.
This is a throughput decision, not a privacy one: parameters are already
redacted as '?' unless EnableSensitiveDataLogging is turned on. To debug a
query, raise this to Information deliberately and lower it again afterwards.
